summary: VitaFAST is a drug discovery program developing first-in-class small-molecule activators of autophagy targeting lysosomal storage disorders (primarily Niemann-Pick type C), longevity/aging, and neurodegeneration. The project is currently at the in vitro lead optimization stage, with three NCE rounds completed, three lead compounds identified at 10-100x higher potency than earlier series, two novel targets identified, and a patent filed for repurposed compounds. A drug repurposing clinical trial pathway via UAE is being scoped alongside IND-enabling studies planned for 2026.

content_blocks.title: Project Overview & Therapeutic Concept
content_blocks.content: Project Title: VitaFAST. Therapeutic concept: Discovery and development of small-molecule activators of autophagy that rescue lysosomal dysfunction and cellular homeostasis. Compounds are identified via high-throughput phenotypic screening in autophagy-deficient cell models and optimized as first-in-class autophagy activators for aging and lysosomal storage disorders. Target Indication: Longevity, Niemann-Pick type C (NPC), and other lysosomal storage disorders. Mechanism of Action: Small molecules that activate autophagy and restore lysosomal function, rescuing cell survival in models with lysosomal dysfunction (Npc1-/-) but not in cells lacking autophagy initiation (Atg5-/-). Biological Target: Autophagy-lysosome pathway.

content_blocks.title: Patient Population & Market Size
content_blocks.content: NPC: Ultra-rare, ~1 per 100,000-120,000 live births globally; ~787 diagnosed prevalent cases in 7 major markets (2022), ~335 in US. NPC therapeutics market ~$110-140M (2024), projected ~$210-260M by 2032. Lysosomal storage disorders (broader): ~1 in 5,000 live births; global LSD therapeutics market ~$9-11B (2025), growing 4.5-8.4% CAGR to ~$13-20B by 2032-2034. Longevity/aging: Universal applicability; global longevity/anti-aging drugs market $8.9B (2023), projected $24.5B by 2032 (11.8% CAGR). Broader neurodegeneration: Alzheimer's (50M+ patients globally), Parkinson's (10M+ globally).

content_blocks.title: Current Development Stage
content_blocks.content: Current stage: Testing new chemical entities (NCEs) in vitro; also exploring feasibility of a drug repurposing clinical trial. Three rounds of NCEs ordered and tested (Q4 2024 – H2 2025). Three lead compounds identified with 10-100x higher potency than previous series. Two novel targets identified (H1 2025) – previously proposed longevity targets. Commercially available compounds binding these targets validated as potent autophagy inducers. Two lead repurposing molecules that have been through Phase 1 trials and are highly potent in lab assays of autophagy.

content_blocks.title: Development Timeline & Milestones
content_blocks.content: Completed milestones: (1) Pilot screening of FDA-approved drug library identified 12 previously unknown autophagy inducers. (2) Thousands of compounds from natural and commercial libraries screened. (3) Multiple hit series with autophagy-activating signatures identified. (4) Three NCE rounds ordered and tested (Q4 2024 – H2 2025). (5) Three lead compounds identified with 10-100x higher potency than previous series. (6) Two novel targets identified (H1 2025). (7) Commercially available compounds binding these targets validated as potent autophagy inducers. Upcoming milestones: Q4 2025 – Complete computational optimization with known targets, IP filing for lead molecules. Q4 2025 – Q1 2026 – Drug repurposing trial scoping (UAE pathway): regulatory pre-submission, CMC planning, clinical protocol draft. 2026 – IND-enabling studies (murine safety experiments) for novel lead compounds. 2026-2027 – Potential Phase 2 clinical trial initiation (repurposed compound pathway).

content_blocks.title: Team Information & Affiliations
content_blocks.content: Key Personnel: Dr. Viktor Korolchuk – Principal Investigator, Cell Biology/Autophagy (Korolchuk Lab, Newcastle University, UK; 160+ peer-reviewed publications, H-index 56, 20,000+ citations). Dr. Peter Banks – High-throughput Screening & Robotics (HTS Facility, Faculty of Medical Sciences, Newcastle University, UK). Dr. Jóhannes Reynisson – Drug Discovery & Medicinal Chemistry/SAR (Keele University, UK). Prof. Konstantin Volcho – Organic & Medicinal Chemistry, Natural-product Library (Novosibirsk Institute of Organic Chemistry, Russian Academy of Sciences, Russia). VitaDAO – decentralized longevity research collective (governance, tokenomics support). Team expertise: autophagy and lysosomal biology, cellular homeostasis and neurodegeneration, high-throughput screening and assay development, organic and medicinal chemistry, SAR and drug discovery, computational chemistry, translational longevity therapeutics.

content_blocks.title: Intellectual Property Status
content_blocks.content: IP strategy under development. IP-NFT registered on Molecule protocol, tokenized as VITA-FAST IP Tokens (first DeSci fractionalized IPT). Newcastle University collaboration IP subject to university IP framework. New patent applications planned for novel compounds developed through SAR optimization (targeting H2 2025). Patent application filed 2nd December 2025 for repurposed compounds for autophagy induction and longevity use – Patent title: 'METHODS FOR ENHANCING AUTOPHAGY USING REPURPOSED PHARMACEUTICAL COMPOUNDS'. IP structure: VitaFast LLC (Delaware) formed to hold and manage project IP.

content_blocks.title: Scope of IP Protection & FTO
content_blocks.content: Filed IP claims: (1) Repurposing claims for commercially available compounds as autophagy activators. (2) Methods of use for treating lysosomal storage disorders via autophagy activation. (3) Methods of use for longevity and age-related disease treatment. Planned claims: composition of matter for novel autophagy-activating small molecules; methods of use for LSD and longevity; novel target applications; screening assays and methods. FTO: Favorable position. VitaFAST targets downstream autophagy activation distinct from mTOR inhibitors (rapamycin, rapalogs). Novel compound structures proprietary and distinct from existing autophagy modulators. Two newly identified targets represent novel mechanism of action. Strong differentiation from existing NPC therapies (miglustat, cyclodextrins).

content_blocks.title: Proof-of-Concept Experimental Data
content_blocks.content: Key experimental results: (1) Autophagy-deficient cells (Npc1-/-, Atg5-/-, Atg7-/-, FIP200/Rb1cc1-/-) show conserved cell-death phenotype under galactose stress; rescue achievable by autophagy induction or downstream interventions (e.g., NAD+ modulation), establishing assay biology. (2) Pilot screen of FDA-approved drugs identified 12 previously unknown autophagy inducers that activate autophagy flux in luciferase-p62 and LC3 'traffic-light' assays, validating the screening platform. (3) Thousands of compounds from natural and commercial libraries screened; multiple hit series with autophagy-activating signatures identified and advanced to derivative synthesis. Disease models: Mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) with Npc1 knockout (Npc1-/-) modelling lysosomal dysfunction associated with NPC and Parkinson's disease. Autophagy-initiation knockouts (Atg5-/-, Atg7-/-, FIP200/Rb1cc1-/-) as negative controls to distinguish true autophagy-dependent rescue from non-specific survival effects.

content_blocks.title: Dose-Response & Potency Data
content_blocks.content: Quantitative dose-response characterization ongoing. Key findings: Third-round NCEs show 10-100x higher potency than earlier lead series. Commercially available compounds binding newly identified targets show highest potency in autophagy assays. Formal EC50/IC50 determination planned as part of lead optimization. Potency benchmarking against rapamycin and other commercial autophagy inducers completed. No specific EC50/IC50 numerical values reported yet.

content_blocks.title: Candidate Status & Safety Data
content_blocks.content: Candidate status: Three lead structures from which variations are producing favorable NCEs. Two lead repurposing molecules that have been through Phase 1 trials and are highly potent in lab assays of autophagy. Preclinical safety (non-GLP): Lead compounds tested in cellular autophagy assays with no acute cytotoxicity signals at therapeutic concentrations. Rescue is specific to autophagy-competent cells (Npc1-/-) and not observed in autophagy-deficient cells (Atg5-/-), demonstrating mechanism specificity. Worm healthspan and longevity studies ongoing to assess systemic effects. Planned safety studies: murine safety experiments as IND-enabling activities; standard ADMET profiling for lead candidates; GLP toxicology package for clinical development.

content_blocks.title: IND Readiness: Manufacturing Route
content_blocks.content: For novel NCEs: Synthesis performed by contracted chemistry suppliers. SAR-driven optimization yielding drug-like molecules. Scale-up synthesis planned following lead selection. Keele University (Dr. Jóhannes Reynisson) providing medicinal chemistry and SAR guidance. Novosibirsk Institute of Organic Chemistry (Prof. Konstantin Volcho) contributing natural product library synthesis. For repurposed compounds: GMP manufacturing scoping initiated (VFDP-14). Manufacturing timeline and cost identified as key risk factors. Existing GMP process for the repurposed compound will be utilized. Regulatory pathway: Clinical trial pathway in UAE. Blood autophagy/mitophagy biomarkers testing as clinical endpoints.

content_blocks.title: Competitive Landscape & Differentiation
content_blocks.content: Key competitors: Rapamycin/Rapalogs (sirolimus, everolimus, temsirolimus) – FDA-approved mTOR inhibitors; significant immunosuppression side effects; work upstream of autophagy. Miglustat (Zavesca/Brazaves) – approved for NPC in EU/Japan (not US); substrate reduction therapy; limited efficacy. Cyclodextrins (Trappsol Cyclo, Kleptose HPB) – compassionate use for NPC; target cholesterol clearance, not autophagy directly. Metformin – AMPK activator; autophagy-inducing effects secondary to metabolic mechanism. VitaFAST differentiation: Novel mechanism via newly identified targets (distinct from mTOR inhibition); lysosomal-specific rescue; 10-100x higher potency than earlier series; addresses autophagy-NAD axis; dual development paths (NCEs + repurposing); first-in-class potential for autophagy activation in longevity.

content_blocks.title: Computational Validation
content_blocks.content: SAR-driven medicinal chemistry optimization across three rounds of NCE synthesis. Computational target analysis following identification of two novel targets (H1 2025). VFDP-15 approved modified plan focusing on computational optimization with known targets. Dr. Jóhannes Reynisson (Keele University) providing drug discovery and SAR analysis.

content_blocks.title: Literature Support & Key Publications
content_blocks.content: Key foundational publications from Korolchuk Lab: (1) Kataura T et al. (2024) 'Targeting the autophagy-NAD axis protects against cell death in Niemann-Pick type C1 disease models' – Cell Death & Disease. (2) Kataura T et al. (2022) 'Autophagy promotes cell survival by maintaining NAD levels' – Developmental Cell. (3) Wilson N et al. (2023) 'The autophagy-NAD axis in longevity and disease' – Trends in Cell Biology. (4) Sedlackova L et al. (2023) 'Metabolic function of autophagy is essential for cell survival' – Autophagy. (5) Sedlackova L & Korolchuk VI (2020) 'The crosstalk of NAD, ROS and autophagy in cellular health and ageing' – Biogerontology. (6) Sun C et al. (2023) 'NAD depletion mediates cytotoxicity in human neurons with autophagy deficiency' – Cell Reports. Target validation: Autophagy dysfunction well-established in NPC, neurodegeneration, and aging. NAD depletion in autophagy deficiency validated across yeast, mouse, and human models.

content_blocks.title: Biomarker Strategy
content_blocks.content: Pharmacodynamic biomarkers: P62 clearance assays (primary autophagy flux measurement); LC3 'traffic-light' assays (autophagy activation confirmation); lysosomal function markers (lysosomal fusion assessment); blood autophagy/mitophagy biomarkers (planned for UAE clinical pathway); NAD levels (metabolic rescue confirmation). Patient stratification for NPC: genetic testing to confirm NPC1/NPC2 mutations; baseline lysosomal function assessment; disease severity staging. Longevity/aging biomarkers for clinical trial: autophagy markers in peripheral blood cells; NAD+ levels in blood; mitochondrial function markers; inflammatory markers.

content_blocks.title: Platform Potential & Strategic Context
content_blocks.content: VitaFAST autophagy activation platform has broad applicability: Neurodegeneration (Alzheimer's – protein aggregate clearance; Parkinson's – mitochondrial quality control; Huntington's disease). Other LSDs beyond NPC (Gaucher, Fabry, mucopolysaccharidoses). Metabolic diseases. Aging/longevity (systemic cellular health maintenance). Cancer (context-dependent autophagy-dependent cell death). Combination approaches with NAD+ precursors (NMN, NR), sirtuin activators, or other geroprotectors.

content_blocks.title: Funding Status
content_blocks.content: Funding history: VitaDAO initial grant (VDP-16): ~$285,000 (project valuation). VITA-FAST Token crowdsale: 1700%+ oversubscribed, ~$620K in bids, ~$32K target sale (1,000,000 tokens minted, 10% sold to community). Ongoing governance-approved budgets: VFDP-11 (Q4 2024), VFDP-12, VFDP-13 ($135K H1 2025), VFDP-14 ($30K repurposing scoping), VFDP-15 (modified H2 2025 plan). Funding model: DeSci/DAO-based with tokenized IP structure.

content_blocks.title: Publications & PI Track Record
content_blocks.content: Viktor Korolchuk: 160+ peer-reviewed publications, H-index 56, 20,000+ citations. Key publications: Nature Cell Death & Disease (2024); Developmental Cell (2022); Trends in Cell Biology (2023). VitaDAO blog posts documenting project progress and milestones. Community update calls (November 2024, ongoing). Conference presentations: VitaDAO community calls and scientific presentations; Newcastle University research seminars. Planned publications: peer-reviewed manuscript on novel autophagy-activating compounds and target identification; conference presentations at aging and lysosomal disease meetings.
